title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: US re-evaluating alliances
sections.summary: The US is re-evaluating its alliances, including NAFTA trade ties with Mexico and Canada and trade with Europe, and voted with Russia and North Korea against a European-led UN resolution condemning Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The US, one of the architects of this system, seems to be re-evaluating its alliances under the current administration, starting with its trade relations with its North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) allies Mexico and Canada, as well as its trading relationship with Europe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the recent vote in the United Nations (UN), the US voted, along with Russia and North Korea, against a resolution put forward by its long-time European allies to condemn the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

sections.label: Rivalry with US intensifying
sections.summary: Its rivalry with the US seems set to intensify on multiple fronts, with the latest salvos being a further round of tariffs against each other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Its rivalry with the US seems set to intensify on multiple fronts, with the latest salvos being a further round of tariffs against each other.

sections.label: Russia-Ukraine war and settlement
sections.summary: The Russia-Ukraine war continues while the US engages both parties to facilitate a settlement, and Ukraine may have to give up parts of its territory in any peace deal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Russia-Ukraine war continues, even as the US has engaged both parties, trying to facilitate some settlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It appears, though, that despite being subject to an unlawful invasion by Russia, Ukraine may have to give up parts of its territory as part of any peace deal.

sections.label: Implications for Singapore's SAF
sections.summary: It has profound implications on the international order and can cause trickle-down effects on small nations like Singapore, so Singapore must stay vigilant and adaptable, integrating emerging technologies to build an SAF that can defend its sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, it has had profound implications on both the international order, and can cause trickle-down effects on small nations like Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is important that we must continue to be vigilant, adaptable, integrating emerging technologies to build an SAF that can defend our sovereignty in times of need, and that is prepared for all contingencies on the modern battlefield.

sections.label: NATO and Asian defence spending
sections.summary: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte urged European members to adopt a wartime mindset and raise defence spending from 2% to 3% of GDP, while the International Institute of Strategic Studies reported expected 4.2% growth in Asian defence spending in 2024, led by China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In December last year, NATO's Secretary-General Mark Rutte exalted NATO's European members to adopt a wartime mindset and increase their defence spending from 2% to 3% of their gross domestic product (GDP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the start of 2024, the International Institute of Strategic Studies reported an expected growth of 4.2% in Asian defence spending, with China leading the way.

sections.label: SAF acquisitions and capability update
sections.summary: It asks whether MINDEF can provide an update on the progress of the SAF's acquisitions and capability development plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF provide an update on the progress of SAF's acquisitions and capability development plans?

sections.label: SAF digital domain threats update
sections.summary: The speaker seeks an update on SAF's progress in addressing threats in the digital domain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to seek an update on SAF's progress in addressing threats in the digital domain.

sections.label: DIS partnering on cyber threats
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the DIS partners with other Government agencies on cyber threats and digital infrastructure security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this in context, I would like to ask the Minister for Defence how the DIS is partnering with other Government agencies to enhance our collective response to cyber threats and ensure the security of our nation's digital infrastructure.

sections.label: SAF unmanned technologies integration
sections.summary: The speaker seeks an update on SAF integrating unmanned technologies into training and operations and plans for threats from them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The cost of using an aerial drone for an attack is relatively small and more difficult to detect, compared to say flying an aeroplane or launching a missile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like an update from the Minister for Defence on how the SAF has been integrating unmanned technologies into its training and operations and its plans on dealing with threats from unmanned technologies.

sections.label: Counter-measure groups and drone threats
sections.summary: The speaker asks for an update on groups developing counter-measure responses and how SAF integrates lessons from recent conflicts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In last year's COS debate, it was highlighted that SAF was going to set up groups to brainstorm and develop sustainable counter-measure responses to this growing threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on the progress of these groups?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: How is SAF integrating lessons from recent conflicts into our own defence planning and what steps are being taken to ensure Singapore remains prepared against these emerging drone attacks and threats?

sections.label: Guarding against disruptive battlefield technology
sections.summary: The speaker asks what MINDEF and SAF are doing to guard against emerging and disruptive technology usable on the battlefield.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given the rapidly changing technological environment, what are MINDEF and SAF doing to guard against these emerging and disruptive technology that can be used on the battlefield?

sections.label: SAFTI City smart training facility
sections.summary: The passage states SAFTI City is a next-generation smart training facility with three Instrumented Battle Circuits and real-time simulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At last year’s COS debate, we learned of SAFTI City – the next-generation smart training facility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Featuring three Instrumented Battle Circuits, SAFTI City will provide immersive, real-time simulations, allowing for video playback as well as comprehensive After Action Reviews.

sections.label: MINDEF land and training areas
sections.summary: MINDEF has freed land for development, and the passage asks what it is doing to maximise local training areas innovatively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, land is a precious and scarce resource for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I note that over the years, MINDEF has done its part to free up land for national development, such as the return of Seletar Camp for the development of the Seletar Aerospace Park and, in time to come, the relocation of Paya Lebar Air Base to transform Paya Lebar into a regional centre similar to those in Woodlands and Tampines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In view of these constraints on our land use in Singapore, what is MINDEF doing to maximise our local training areas in an innovative manner?

sections.label: Benefits of overseas training
sections.summary: Overseas training fosters defence ties, improves bilateral cooperation and allows benchmarking against other professional militaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Training overseas also helps to foster strong defence ties with our key defence partners, improve bilateral cooperation and allow us to benchmark ourselves against other professional militaries.

sections.label: Paya Lebar noise and fin nozzles
sections.summary: Residents report up to seven flights an hour, with relief after Paya Lebar Air Base decommissioning in 2030, and fin line nozzles offered as a solution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Some residents even suggest that the frequency of such incidents may number as many as seven flights an hour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The responses, while lengthy and varied, have largely retained the same thrust that the Air Force needs to maintain operational readiness for the good of national defence and that there will eventually be relief after the decommissioning of Paya Lebar Air Base sometime in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Technology, however, has now offered a tested solution, fin line nozzles that can be incorporated into engine design, much like dimples on a golf ball.

sections.label: Defence spending early years
sections.summary: Defence has always been prioritised with adequate financial and manpower resources, and early defence spending was about 5% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have always prioritised defence, ensuring that there are adequate financial and manpower resources committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I looked up our defence spending in our early years as a young nation and, back then, defence spending was in the range of about 5% of GDP.

sections.label: Staying within 3% GDP
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore will continue to stay within the range of 3% of GDP with high-end capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the acquisition of high-end capabilities, will we continue to stay within the range of 3% of our GDP?

sections.label: Hybrid warfare threats
sections.summary: Hybrid warfare blends conventional forces with cyberattacks, disinformation and economic coercion, threatening infrastructure, communications, trade and energy supplies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Hybrid warfare, blending conventional forces with cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns and economic coercion, has become a key tool for state and non-state actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Cyber warfare threatens critical infrastructure while economic sabotage, such as cutting of submarine cables, can severely disrupt vital communications, trade and energy supplies.

sections.label: Regional counter-terrorism cooperation agreement
sections.summary: Through REACT, member countries exchange information, track terror group movements and disrupt terrorist plots.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Through initiatives, like the Regional Cooperation Agreement on Combating Terrorism (REACT), member countries exchange information, track terror group movements and disrupt terrorist plots.

sections.label: US and Australia partnerships
sections.summary: Cooperation with the US includes joint operations and intelligence sharing against transnational threats, while partnership with Australia supports humanitarian relief and peacekeeping.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our cooperation with US includes joint operations and intelligence sharing to counter transnational threats, such as cyberattacks and weapon proliferation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, our partnership with Australia supports collaborative initiatives in humanitarian relief and peacekeeping.

sections.label: Redesigning medical and PES systems
sections.summary: In 2021, Senior Minister of State Heng said SAF is redesigning the Medical Classification System and PES system to maximise servicemen's deployment options and contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2021, Senior Minister of State Heng shared that SAF is redesigning the Medical Classification System and the Physical Employment Standard (PES) system to maximise the deployment options and contributions of our servicemen.

sections.label: NSmen skills and polytechnic enlistment scheme
sections.summary: Tapping NSmen's skills enhances SAF's operational capabilities, and a scheme lets polytechnic students enlist while serving final-year internships; it asks if this expanded and the take-up rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This not only optimises their potential but also enhances SAF's operational capabilities by tapping on the skills and expertise of our NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I note that the newest scheme that was launched last year allows polytechnic students to enlist and serve in SAF while fulfilling their final-year internship requirements for their diplomas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Has this scheme been expanded to include more domains and what is the take-up rate?

sections.label: Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme announcement
sections.summary: MINDEF previously announced it sought to maximise NSmen contributions through the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: MINDEF previously announced that they sought to maximise contributions of NSmen through the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sections.label: Update on Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme
sections.summary: It asks MINDEF for an update on the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme and how it has helped maximise NSmen contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme and how it has helped to maximise the contributions of our NSmen?

sections.label: MINDEF SAF servicemen operational effectiveness
sections.summary: Asks what ongoing MINDEF/SAF efforts equip servicemen to do their roles well and enhance operational effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this context, what are the ongoing efforts by MINDEF/SAF to ensure that our servicemen are equipped to do their roles well and to enhance their operational effectiveness?

sections.label: SAF training safety and realism
sections.summary: Asks what recent SAF steps improve training safety while maintaining realism and effectiveness, and how safety protocols are benchmarked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: What are the recent steps that the SAF has taken to improve training safety and yet maintain training realism and effectiveness?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: How are we benchmarking our safety protocols against industry and global military best practices?

sections.label: Technology in training efficacy safety
sections.summary: Asks MINDEF to share how technology has been incorporated to improve training efficacy and safety of servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Can MINDEF share more about how technology has been incorporated to improve training efficacy and safety of our servicemen?

sections.label: Soldiers mental health support update
sections.summary: Asks MINDEF for an update on efforts to ensure all soldiers have adequate mental health support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask MINDEF for an update on efforts to ensure that all our soldiers have adequate mental health support.

sections.label: New CMPB regional health hub
sections.summary: States the new CMPB would house a regional health hub centralising SAF healthcare facilities spread across multiple locations.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Apart from the one-stop service centre, all-weather fitness conditioning centre, and the lifestyle mart, the new CMPB would also house a regional health hub that would centralise the various SAF healthcare facilities that are spread across multiple locations, including the Medical Classification Centre, Specialist Medical and Dental Centre, Health Screening Programme Centre and MINDEF Medical Centre.

sections.label: Raising median NS allowance
sections.summary: States the median NS allowance should be raised to at least $1,600 monthly, noting second-year NSFs receive an allowance, not salary with CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The median NS allowance should be raised to at least $1,600 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NSFs in their second year are fully trained, performing operational roles essential to Singapore security, yet they continue to receive an allowance rather than a salary with Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions.

sections.label: NSF education and career transition
sections.summary: MINDEF should coordinate with universities to reduce delays between NSFs' Operationally Ready Date and studies, and include career-beneficial training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MINDEF should also help NSFs transition smoothly to further education by coordinating with universities to reduce delays between their Operationally Ready Date and the start of their studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And finally, NS should where possible, incorporate training that can benefits NSFs future careers, including skills training that can be applied in both military and civilian settings.

sections.label: SkillsFuture@NS enhanced initiatives
sections.summary: MINDEF announced enhanced SkillsFuture@NS initiatives giving full-time NSmen access to the SF@NS LXP with over 75,000 online courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: At last year's Committee of Supply debate, MINDEF announced enhanced SkillsFuture@NS initiatives, allowing full-time NSmen access to the SSkillsFuture@NS Learning eXperience Platform (SF@NS LXP), which offers over 75,000 online courses.

sections.label: Total Defence and Exercise SG Ready
sections.summary: Total Defence rallies Singaporeans as one united people, and Exercise SG Ready 2025 had over 800 organisations, schools and units carry out disruption activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: That is why Total Defence is key in rallying Singaporeans together to combat the challenges ahead as one united people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We just concluded Exercise SG Ready 2025, a two-week exercise where more than 800 organisations, schools and units from different sectors carried out different disruption or preparedness activities to strengthen their contingency plans for power disruptions or phishing attacks.

sections.label: Exercise SG Ready update request
sections.summary: Hospitals faced delayed critical procedures, and the member requests an update on this year's Exercise SG Ready and other crisis preparedness initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Hospitals have been forced into crisis mode, with critical medical procedures delayed or disrupted, underscoring the grave consequences when essential services are compromised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: This year’s edition of Exercise SG Ready, held in February, built on those lessons learnt from last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: In light of SG60, I would like to request an update from the Ministry on this year’s exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Could MINDEF also share other initiatives that are underway to further strengthen Singapore’s crisis preparedness so that our nation remains resilient and well-guarded against emerging threats?

sections.label: Public trust and societal resilience
sections.summary: The member asks MINDEF about efforts beyond conventional warfare to strengthen society's resilience in dealing with emergencies or crises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: We also need to build public trust in our Government, public services and emergency response systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: I wish to ask MINDEF, beyond preparing for conventional warfare, could MINDEF share more about its efforts in strengthening our society’s resilience in dealing with emergencies or crises?

sections.label: Total Defence discussions with youths
sections.summary: The member asks how MINDEF is fostering and enabling discussions on Total Defence, particularly with youths.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: With this in mind, I would like to ask how MINDEF is fostering and enabling discussions on Total Defence, particularly with our youths?

sections.label: MINDEF activity outcomes summary
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MINDEF would provide a summary of the outcomes of the activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Would MINDEF provide a summary of the outcomes of the activities?

sections.label: Update on ACCORD initiatives
sections.summary: The passage requests an update from the Ministry of Defence on ACCORD, its initiatives and activities over the past year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Given the evolving security landscape, I would like to request an update from the Ministry of Defence on ACCORD, their initiatives and activities over the past year.

sections.label: MINDEF/SAF innovation in Total Defence
sections.summary: The passage asks how MINDEF/SAF is encouraging innovation in Total Defence amid new and evolving threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: In the face of new and evolving threats, how is MINDEF/SAF encouraging innovation in Total Defence?

sections.label: Shift from liberal to literal order
sections.summary: The passage states a move from a liberal world order to a literal world order based on size, influence and power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: From a liberal world order characterised by inclusion, rules for large and small states and a protection of the global commons, we have now moved from that liberal world order to a literal world order based on size and influence, based on power.

sections.label: Fates of nations, 1824 treaty
sections.summary: The passage says history teaches that fates of nations, particularly weak ones, can change without their choice, citing the 1824 Anglo-Dutch Treaty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: History teaches us that the fates of nations, particularly the weak ones – and I use the word "nations" in the broadest sense – can change without their choice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Take the 1824 Anglo-Dutch Treaty, when Singapore and Malaysia came under British rule.

sections.label: Sykes-Picot secret agreement 1916
sections.summary: The passage describes the 1916 Sykes-Picot secret agreement between the French and British dividing the Ottoman Empire's remnants, made public after the Bolsheviks discovered it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Or fates of nations decided by others unannounced, without the knowledge of the affected states or the nations most affected, as in the Sykes-Picot agreement, secret agreement in 1916, between the French and the British, when they decided to divide up the remnants of the Ottoman Empire, and it was only because the Bolsheviks discovered it a year later, and then it was made public.

sections.label: Japan Pearl Harbor attack
sections.summary: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 under its Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As it did for this region on 7 December 1941, when Japan attacked Pearl Harbor under their strategy for a Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere.

sections.label: Invincible-class submarine construction
sections.summary: In 2017, Singapore started building four Invincible-class submarines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: You remember in 2017, we started building four Invincible-class submarines.

sections.label: Submarine fleet and MRCV plans
sections.summary: The SAF plans to procure two more Invincible-class submarines for a total of six, and the Navy will launch its first MRCV.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Having proven that the Invincible-class submarines can perform to expectations in tropical waters, the SAF plans to procure two more submarines to make up a total of six as a steady state for our submarine fleet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Navy will also launch its first multi-role combat vessel (MRCV) later this year.

sections.label: Additional F-35A acquisition
sections.summary: At last year's COS, the decision was announced to acquire eight more F-35As, besides the 12 F-35Bs previously announced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: At last year's COS, I announced our decision to acquire eight more F-35As, in addition to the 12 F-35Bs we had previously announced.

sections.label: Titan firepower upgrade
sections.summary: The Titan will remain wheeled but will for the first time have its firepower upgraded with a 30 millimetre cannon as a remote weapon system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Titan will still be wheeled, but for the first time, it will have its firepower upgraded with a 30 millimetre cannon as a remote weapon system.

sections.label: Digital and Intelligence Service formation
sections.summary: The DIS was formed in 2022 as a culmination of reorganisation efforts to better meet future digital needs and threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The DIS was formed in 2022 and indeed it is one culmination of efforts in the reorganisation so that they could better meet future needs and threats in the digital sphere.

sections.label: SAF C4 Digitalisation Command
sections.summary: The passage names the SAF C4 and Digitalisation Command (SAFC4DC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: First, the SAF C4 and Digitalisation Command (SAFC4DC).

sections.label: Defence Cyber Command consolidation
sections.summary: DCCOM will consolidate all cybersecurity operations and capabilities and partner with whole-of-Government and industry to strengthen national cyber defence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The second new DIS command is the Defence Cyber Command (DCCOM), which will consolidate all cybersecurity operations and capabilities, and partner with whole-of-Government and industry to strengthen national cyber defence.

sections.label: Ukraine drone production study
sections.summary: A Kyiv School of Economics study showed Ukraine can now produce four million drones annually, a hundred-fold increase from before its war with Russia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: A study by the Kyiv School of Economics showed that Ukraine is now capable of producing four million drones annually, a hundred-fold increase from before their war with Russia.

sections.label: Army Drone Accelerator office
sections.summary: The Army will establish the Drone Accelerator for Rapid Equipping (DARE), a similar office to scale up UAV and ground vehicle operations across the Army.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Army will also establish the Drone Accelerator for Rapid Equipping (DARE) a similar office to scale up operations for UAVs and ground vehicles for its units across the Army.

sections.label: SAF counter-UAS capabilities group
sections.summary: The SAF will build counter-UAS capabilities and a new SAF Counter-UAS Development and Operations group to guard against the threat with other Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: They can be re-tooled as weapons to inflict harm and destruction, for example, terrorists could do that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: So, to meet this threat, the SAF will build new counter-UAS capabilities – a suite of sensors, jammers and weapon solutions to detect and neutralise smaller UASs, to add to our existing Island Air Defence capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: A newly established SAF Counter-UAS Development and Operations group will be responsible to guard against this threat in collaboration with other Government agencies.

sections.label: Drone attack defence cost
sections.summary: The passage states that 100 attacking drones cost about $15 million while defending against them would cost nearly $250 million, which is unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: If the aggressor fires 100 drones, it will cost about $15 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But to defend against them would cost nearly $250 million; clearly unsustainable.

sections.label: Combined SAF training area
sections.summary: The combined training area with Greenvale Training Area will be 10 times Singapore's size, allowing up to 14,000 personnel and 2,400 vehicles annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: After the development of the adjacent Greenvale Training Area, the SAF will have a combined training area 10 times the size of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This combined training area will allow us to deploy up to 14,000 personnel and 2,400 vehicles annually, so that the SAF can exercise its full range of capabilities, land, sea, air and digital.

sections.label: Defence expenditure increase
sections.summary: Financial expenditure is projected at around $23.4 billion, a 12.4% increase from last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Through them, we turn our people’s hard-earned monies into tangible benefits, tangible bulwarks to protect Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This financial expenditure is projected to be around $23.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It is a 12.4% increase from last year.

sections.label: Defence spending within GDP range
sections.summary: Defence spending stayed within 3% of GDP over the past decade and is expected to taper from FY2026, barring major conflicts or severe economic uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Even so, over the past decade, defence spending has stayed within the range of 3% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I expect the growth in defence spending to taper down from FY2026 and keep within this 3% of GDP range over the next decade, of course, barring any major conflicts or severe economic uncertainty.

sections.label: Inaugural PATKOR INDOPURA air patrol
sections.summary: Both Air Forces will conduct the inaugural bilateral air patrol under the Singapore-Indonesia Coordinated Patrol later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Both Air Forces, for example, will conduct the inaugural bilateral air patrol under the Singapore-Indonesia Coordinated Patrol (PATKOR INDOPURA) later this year.

sections.label: 1990 MOU extended 15 years
sections.summary: The 2019 Protocol of Amendment extended the 1990 MOU for another 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The 2019 Protocol of Amendment extended the 1990 MOU for another 15 years.

sections.label: RHCC aid delivery to Gaza
sections.summary: In March last year, RHCC coordinated aid supplies to Gaza via Jordan using an A330 MRTT, a C-130 and a commercial plane.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In March last year, RHCC coordinated a delivery of aid supplies to Gaza via Jordan and used our A330 Multi-Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) aircraft, a C-130 transport aircraft and a commercial plane.

sections.label: Gaza civilians treatment regional options
sections.summary: Civilians from Gaza have received treatment in Egypt, Jordan or the UAE, and SAF and MOH medical teams may deploy to such a place in coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But there are other options in the region, whether it is in Egypt, Jordan or the United Arab Emirates (UAE), as more civilians from Gaza have gone to receive treatment over the past months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We have already seen that and the SAF medical teams, together with the Ministry of Health (MOH) medical teams, may be able to deploy to such a place in the coming months.

sections.label: Regional CBR Centre in Singapore
sections.summary: MINDEF/SAF will establish a regional CBR Centre in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: MINDEF/SAF will therefore establish a regional CBR Centre in Singapore.

sections.label: Maximum Containment Facility certification 2026
sections.summary: The facility will complete construction in 2026 and be certified as a Maximum Containment Facility under WHO and MOH guidelines to handle highly contagious and lethal bio-agents such as Ebola.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I think the reaction to that was quite muted and I think because it was after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We all saw the need for it and this facility will complete construction in 2026 and, in line with WHO and MOH guidelines, it will be certified as a Maximum Containment Facility (MCF), the highest grade, to be able to handle bio-agents that are deemed highly contagious and lethal, such as the Ebola virus.

sections.label: Redesigning SAF medical classification
sections.summary: In 2021, the SAF was said to be redesigning medical classification of servicemen, shifting away from Combat Fit or Non-Combat Fit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In 2021, I shared that the SAF is redesigning the way we medically classify our servicemen, shifting away from the binary classification of servicemen as either being Combat Fit or Non-Combat Fit.

sections.label: Pre-enlistees functional assessments outcomes
sections.summary: Since 2022, about 300 pre-enlistees underwent selected functional assessments, and 230, about two-thirds, contributed more effectively over a wider range of roles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since 2022, some 300 pre-enlistees have undergone selected functional assessments, and 230, or about two-thirds of them, were able to contribute more effectively over a wider range of roles.

sections.label: Servicemen in redesigned operational roles
sections.summary: Since 2021, more than 1,000 servicemen have taken on operational roles such as Combat Medics, Infantry Carrier Vehicle Operators and Military Police that they would not have been eligible for without redesign.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since 2021, more than 1,000 servicemen have taken on important operational roles, such as Combat Medics, Infantry Carrier Vehicle Operators and Military Police, which they would not have been able, or been eligible for if the roles were not redesigned.

sections.label: Redeploying NSmen civilian expertise
sections.summary: The Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme has redeployed over 600 NSmen in three years using their civilian expertise and qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Under the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme (EEDS), we have redeployed more than 600 NSmen over the past three years by tapping on their civilian expertise and qualifications.

sections.label: SAF medical responsiveness and ambulances
sections.summary: The SAF will acquire a new fleet of ambulances with mechanical chest compression devices and powered stretchers to enhance medical responsiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Such experiences sharpen our medics' clinical skills and ensure that they are well-prepared to respond to emergencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We will enhance the SAF's medical responsiveness by acquiring a new fleet of ambulances, which are equipped with mechanical chest compression devices and powered stretchers, similar to the ambulances used by SCDF.

sections.label: Inspector-General's Office safety audits
sections.summary: The Inspector-General's Office, established in 2019, conducts 40 to 50 audits and system reviews yearly to ensure safety protocol adherence in SAF Formations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Inspector-General's Office (IGO), established in 2019, conducts 40 to 50 audits and system reviews every year to ensure adherence to safety protocols in SAF Formations.

sections.label: Fourth ERPSS training safety review
sections.summary: The fourth ERPSS, inaugurated in May 2024, will continue reviewing selected SAF Formations' training to help the SAF benchmark against best practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: To help the SAF benchmark against best practices and standards in training safety, the fourth ERPSS, inaugurated in May 2024, will continue to review selected SAF Formations' training.

sections.label: Army AI safety transgression model
sections.summary: The Army used AI to develop a model that recognises and detects safety transgressions in activities such as live-firing in ranges and driving.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Army also leveraged AI to develop a model that recognises and detects safety transgressions in activities, such as live-firing in ranges and driving.

sections.label: Army Resilience Centre mental resilience
sections.summary: The Army Resilience Centre, established in March 2024, partners training centres and units on resilience-training curriculums to bolster Servicemen's mental resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Army Resilience Centre (AReC), established in March 2024, partners Army training centres and units in implementing structured resilience-training curriculums and redesigning training programmes to bolster Servicemen's mental resilience and adjustment to military life.

sections.label: NS preparation information guides
sections.summary: Since May 2024, NS preparation information guides have been available to pre-enlistees and parents on the LifeSG app and website.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since May 2024, information guides on preparation for NS have been made available to pre-enlistees and their parents on the LifeSG app and website.

sections.label: Smart Mobilisation system on OneNS
sections.summary: In March 2024, the Smart Mobilisation system was onboarded to the OneNS app for selected SAF units, to be extended to all by year-end.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In March 2024, the Smart Mobilisation system, which digitises mobilisation status in real-time, was onboarded to the OneNS app for selected SAF units.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This will be extended to all SAF units by the end of the year.

sections.label: New CMPB opening
sections.summary: The new CMPB will open progressively from the middle of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The new CMPB will open progressively from the middle of 2025.

sections.label: NSF monthly allowance increase
sections.summary: From 1 July this year, NSF monthly allowances will rise by $35 to $75, giving $790 to $1,955 depending on rank and vocation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Following our latest review, we will raise our NSFs' monthly allowances by between $35 to $75 from 1 July this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: With the change, NSFs will receive a monthly allowance of between $790 and $1,955, depending on their rank and vocation.

sections.label: NSF skills and training support
sections.summary: NSFs attend SkillsFuture@NS Fairs and can use the Learning eXperience Platform, with about half signed up since Nov 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: NSFs attend the SkillsFuture@NS Fairs which, aside from providing job opportunities in growing industries, also feature workshops that provide them with resources and tools for skills planning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For NSFs who prefer self-directed training, the Learning eXperience Platform (LXP) offers a range of courses from data analytics to self-management and interpersonal communications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since Nov 2022, about half of our NSFs have signed up for accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as we look forward, MINDEF/SAF’s commitment to NS and to our NSmen remains steadfast.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We will continue to enhance the NS experience, maximise the contributions of our NSmen, and strengthen recognition for their service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Most importantly, we will uphold the safety and well-being of every soldier, ensuring that they return home safely to their loved ones.

sections.label: New SAFRA Bayshore clubhouse
sections.summary: MINDEF will build SAFRA Bayshore, its largest clubhouse, to replace SAFRA Tampines and be ready in a few years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, the seven SAFRA clubhouses across Singapore provide servicemen and their families with affordable recreational facilities and lifestyle offerings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that MINDEF will build a new clubhouse in the Bayshore area, to better serve our servicemen and their families in the East.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Ms Denise Phua had asked for an update and she will be pleased to know that SAFRA Bayshore will be SAFRA’s largest clubhouse, about 50% larger than the average SAFRA clubhouse, and will offer unique family, entertainment and recreational facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We plan for SAFRA Bayshore to be ready in a few years’ time, and to replace our oldest clubhouse at SAFRA Tampines, built in 1988.

sections.label: Exercise SG Ready power disruptions
sections.summary: MINDEF and the Energy Market Authority held the second Exercise SG Ready, with over 1,200 organisations participating.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over the past two weeks, MINDEF, together with the Energy Market Authority, conducted the second edition of Exercise SG Ready, focused on enhancing community preparedness for power disruptions and cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year, over 1,200 organisations participated in the exercise, including schools, communities, businesses and Government agencies.

sections.label: SAF solar panel deployment target
sections.summary: Singapore committed in 2021 to deploy more solar panels in SAF camps and bases, targeting 50 mega-watt peak by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To reduce our carbon emissions growth, we had committed in 2021 to deploy more solar panels in SAF camps and bases, to achieve a target of 50 mega-watt peak of solar capacity by 2025, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of 13,000 4-room Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats.

sections.label: Sembawang Air Base solar farm
sections.summary: A solar farm with 18 mega-watt peak solar photovoltaic systems will be built within Sembawang Air Base this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: On top of that, we will be building a solar farm within Sembawang Air Base this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The solar farm will comprise 18 mega-watt peak solar photovoltaic systems and will generate energy equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of 4,700 four-room HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This will lead to cost savings of approximately $1.9 million a year for the SAF and bring us closer to achieving our emissions reduction target for 2030.

sections.label: Total Defence pledges by Singaporeans
sections.summary: Over 300,000 Singaporeans were encouraged to reflect and make pledges in support of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over 300,000 Singaporeans were encouraged to reflect and make pledges in support of Total Defence.

sections.label: ACCORD engagement with businesses and SMEs
sections.summary: ACCORD will focus this year on engaging businesses, particularly SMEs, using the MINDEF-SBF memorandum of understanding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: ACCORD has existing programmes reaching out to pre-enlistees, youths, new citizens, Permanent Residents (PRs), national servicemen, families and women.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year, ACCORD will focus on engaging businesses, particularly SMEs, leveraging on the memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed between MINDEF and the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) last month.

sections.label: Virtual BMTC visits for pre-enlistees
sections.summary: Virtual visits will open to all pre-enlistees enlisting in 2026 and their families after good feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Following good feedback from the attendees, we will open the virtual visits to all pre-enlistees enlisting in 2026 along with their families to allow more family members to take part in the BMTC tour and understand more about the importance of NS.

sections.label: Cadet CPR-AED training
sections.summary: Over two years, over 10,000 cadets have undergone CPR-AED training and gained emergency preparedness skills for community medical emergencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over the past two years, over 10,000 cadets have undergone CPR-AED training and have been equipped with emergency preparedness skills to react to critical medical emergencies in the community.

sections.label: Refreshed museum opening 2026
sections.summary: The public can look forward to visiting the refreshed museum in early 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The public can look forward to visiting the refreshed museum in early 2026.

sections.label: Innovative proposals received
sections.summary: Through the programme, a total of 258 innovative proposals have been received.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Through the programme, we have received a total of 258 innovative proposals.

sections.label: Deployment duration and options
sections.summary: They are prepared for a number of weeks or even months if needed, and could deploy on land or use a hospital ship.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In terms of duration, we are prepared for a number of weeks or even months, if there is a need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We could also deploy on land or use a hospital ship.

sections.label: Local ship development option
sections.summary: If there is an option to develop locally, they will explore it; the first ship was produced with DCN, but the subsequent five were built locally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If there is an option to develop locally, obviously, we will explore the option.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The first ship was produced together with the French Direction des Constructions Navales (DCN), but the subsequent five ships were built locally – as we are also building for a number of naval platforms.

sections.label: Defence spending GDP peg
sections.summary: The member agrees on steady defence spending for operational readiness but asks whether MOF budget requests are pegged to GDP and if the peg shifted from 5% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I agree with the need for steady defence spending to maintain operational readiness, but can the Minister clarify whether the budget requests from MOF each year is actually pegged to Singapore's GDP?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And has this peg shifted from 5% to 3% of GDP over the years and, if so, how has this been justified?

sections.label: CPF contributions for NSFs
sections.summary: A question asks whether MINDEF has considered making CPF contributions to NSFs for retirement adequacy, and whether defence dollars follow GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Has MINDEF considered making CPF contributions to NSFs to support their retirement adequacy?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think the primary question is does MINDEF seek defence dollars based on how the GDP goes.

sections.label: NS allowance and CPF
sections.summary: The NS allowance is an honorarium so CPF is not payable, but NS HOME Awards include CPF and cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: The NS allowance, the nature of it, it is in a form of honorarium and for that, CPF is not payable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: One, within the NS journey, they are actually eligible for NS HOME Awards, which are paid out in the course of the NSmen's journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Those actually come in a mixture of CPF as well as cash.

sections.label: Thanks to Minister's speech
sections.summary: A member thanks the Minister for an extensive and detailed speech on geopolitical and military matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank the Minister for his speech earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: It was quite extensive and detailed, especially on the geopolitical and military front.

sections.label: Not business as usual
sections.summary: The speaker says it is not business as usual when the transatlantic relationship, NATO and the US position are in question.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And my overall point is not business as usual.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is not business as usual when the transatlantic relationship is threatened.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is not business as usual when people question whether NATO can survive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is not business as usual when the US takes a different position and the US vote in the way that it did, compared to previously.

sections.label: Back to fundamentals
sections.summary: The speaker lists fundamentals: a united people, strong SAF, strong security, working economy and strong fiscal position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: You have to go back to the fundamentals, a united people, a strong SAF, strong security, a working economy, a strong fiscal Budget, a strong fiscal position.

sections.label: A330 Gaza delivery cost
sections.summary: The speaker notes that sending an A330 Multi-Role Tanker Transport to deliver goods to Gaza cost more than commercial means.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For example, when we send an A330 Multi-Role Tanker Transport to deliver goods to Gaza, it would have been less costly to send by commercial means.
